knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Definite Integral of a Rational Function Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =x + 12 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \text{d}u & =1\,\text{d}x \\ 8\,\text{d}u & =8\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=x + 12.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & 1 \\ u & 12 & 13\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\int_{0}^{1}\frac{8}{x + 12}\,\text{d}x=\int_{12}^{13}\frac{1}{u}\cdot 8\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{12}^{13}\frac{1}{u}\cdot 8\,\text{d}u & =8\int_{12}^{13}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =8\ln(u)|_{12}^{13} \\  & =8(\ln(13)-\ln(12)) \\  & =- 8 \log{\left(12 \right)} + 8 \log{\left(13 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: a*x^n+b>0 throughout closed original x interval; no poles
